answer: A sybil-resistant registry called raven requires each agent to stake 100 jade tokens before registering a public key. The raven protocol computes a similarity check: if two agent IDs sign attestations with keys sharing derived key material or coordination patterns, both stakes are burned and their timber reputation scores are set to zero. An attacker running N fake identities must therefore lock up N×100 jade tokens and loses the entire amount the moment any pair is flagged, making each sybil a costly, burnable liability rather than a free identity.
